prompt.context_jp: 「桑野さんに"好きだ"って」
prompt.prompt_jp: 桑野さん___「好きだ」って言っちゃいました。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that marks the person the confession was said TO.

feedback.correct_en: に marks Kuwano-san as the recipient of the quoted words — the target she spoke to.
feedback.incorrect_en: を would treat Kuwano-san as a direct object (not possible with 言う this way), and が would make him the subject.

contrast_examples.en: I handed the book to him.

prompt.context_jp: みちるの告白の話をしている文脈。
prompt.prompt_jp: みちるちゃんの気持ち___ 桑野さんに全然伝わってないみたい。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking 'Michiru-chan's feelings' as the topic under discussion.

feedback.correct_en: The speaker is commenting ON Michiru's feelings as the established topic — は fits this topic-continuation role.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce it as new information (not the case — they've been discussing it), and を doesn't work with 伝わる (intransitive).

contrast_examples.jp: この話は彼に伝わっていない。

contrast_examples.en: A strange sound was heard (new info).

prompt.context_jp: 桑野のテレビでの発言。
prompt.prompt_jp: 建築家の個性___ 発揮されて 初めていい家ができるんです。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking '建築家の個性' in this conditional clause.

feedback.correct_en: Inside a subordinate 〜て初めて clause, the subject of 発揮される takes が — it's presented as a condition being newly introduced.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would wrongly promote 'the architect's individuality' to a top-level topic, breaking the subordinate structure.

contrast_examples.jp: 努力が実って成功した。
contrast_examples.en: The effort bore fruit and it succeeded.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼の個性はすばらしい。

prompt.context_jp: 母が桑野に語る場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: あなた___ ホントの独りぼっちを知らないのよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking 'あなた' — the mother is contrasting him with others.

feedback.correct_en: The mother sets up 'you' as the topic she wants to tell something about — a contrastive/topic は. She's saying 'YOU (unlike me) don't know real loneliness.'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it answer 'who doesn't know?' as new info, but the focus here is on what she tells him about himself.

contrast_examples.jp: あなたは分かってない。

prompt.context_jp: 母の病室で。
prompt.prompt_jp: やっぱり あなたの結婚のこと___ 考えちゃった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking 'あなたの結婚のこと' as what she was thinking about.

feedback.correct_en: 考える takes を for the thing being thought about — 'your marriage' is the direct object of her thinking.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would sound like her marriage itself was acting, and に doesn't match 考える for 'think about'.

prompt.context_jp: 母が桑野に言う。
prompt.prompt_jp: 桑野家でテレビ出演は あなた___ 初めてね。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: she's identifying him as the FIRST in the family to appear on TV.

feedback.correct_en: This identifies 'you' as the one (among all family members) who is first — an exhaustive/identifying が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would just make him a topic without the 'you specifically are the first' nuance. も would mean 'also,' which contradicts 'first.'

contrast_examples.jp: この中で彼が一番若い。
contrast_examples.en: Among these, HE is the youngest.

prompt.context_jp: 夏美が実験の話を聞いて。
prompt.prompt_jp: みちるちゃん___ 桑野のことを…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle introducing Michiru's feelings as newly revealed information.

feedback.correct_en: Natsumi is just learning this — Michiru's feelings for Kuwano are new information being introduced, so が fits.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose Michiru as an established topic of the current exchange, but Natsumi is reacting to a just-revealed fact.

contrast_examples.jp: 実はあの子が彼を好きなの。

prompt.context_jp: 母が桑野に。
prompt.prompt_jp: 近く___ 誰かいるでしょう？ いつも。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking location of existence.

feedback.correct_en: いる (existence) takes に for the location where someone exists — 'someone is NEARBY.'
feedback.incorrect_en: で marks the location of an action, not of existence. を marks a path or object.

contrast_examples.en: There's a cat in the room.

prompt.context_jp: 桑野の建築哲学。
prompt.prompt_jp: 私の場合 キッチン___ 重視した設計をしておりまして。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 'the kitchen' as the thing being emphasized.

feedback.correct_en: 重視する is transitive — the kitchen is the direct object being prioritized, so を.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make the kitchen the subject (it isn't doing anything here), and に would suggest a destination.

prompt.context_jp: 夏美が自分の気持ちを告げる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 私___ キャッチボールがしてみたいです あなたと。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking 私 in this pivotal line.

feedback.correct_en: Natsumi contrasts herself with the previous dodgeball-only dynamic — 'I (for my part) want to play catch.' Topical/contrastive は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would answer 'who wants to play catch?' as new info, but the focus is her declaration about herself as topic.

prompt.context_jp: 桑野がやっと気持ちを口にする。
prompt.prompt_jp: 僕は… あなた___ 好きなんじゃないかな？
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking 'あなた' as the object of 好き.

feedback.correct_en: 〜が好きだ: the target of liking is marked with が. '僕は' sets the topic (me), and 'あなたが' names what I like.
feedback.incorrect_en: を is a common learner error — 好き is an adjective, not a transitive verb, so it takes が. は would double-topic awkwardly.

contrast_examples.jp: 私はコーヒーが好きだ。

prompt.context_jp: 二人は実はお似合い、という話。
prompt.prompt_jp: 信介___ その気になるかどうかなのよね。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking Shinsuke in 'it depends on whether HE feels that way.'

feedback.correct_en: Inside the embedded か-clause ('whether Shinsuke feels that way'), the subject takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside such an embedded yes/no clause would feel like a top-level topic, breaking the structure.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼が来るかどうか分からない。
contrast_examples.en: I don't know whether he'll come.

prompt.context_jp: 桑野が気づきを語る。
prompt.prompt_jp: やっと できない理由___ 分かったんです。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking 'the reason I couldn't' as what became clear.

feedback.correct_en: 分かる takes が for what becomes understood — and here 'the reason' is newly grasped information.
feedback.incorrect_en: を is a common error — 分かる is intransitive and takes が, not を. は would wrongly topicalize.

prompt.context_jp: 桑野がみちるに。
prompt.prompt_jp: 自己責任だろう そんなこと___ 言いに来たのか？
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking 'such a thing' as what she came to say.

feedback.correct_en: 言う takes を for its content — 'that kind of thing' is the direct object of 言いに来る.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it the subject, and に would turn it into a destination.

prompt.context_jp: 「最初は あんまり 好きじゃないっていうか」「でも 今は あの… ___っていうか」
prompt.prompt_jp: 最初は嫌いだったけど、今は ___ っていうか。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word fits the contrast with 'disliked at first'?

feedback.correct_en: 逆 ('the opposite') cleanly flips 'disliked' into 'liked' — matching her confession to Kuwano.
feedback.incorrect_en: 同じ would mean 'same' (contradicting 'but now...'), and 普通 ('normal') wouldn't convey a reversal.

prompt.context_jp: 告白を断られて。
prompt.prompt_jp: 二度と 人を ___ なったりしません。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that completes 'fall in love with someone.'

feedback.correct_en: 好きになる ('come to like / fall for') uses に to mark the resulting state. '人を好きに なる' is the fixed pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: が and を don't work here — なる (become) requires に to mark the state you become.

contrast_examples.jp: 好きになってしまった。
contrast_examples.en: I ended up falling for them.

prompt.context_jp: 桑野が反発して。
prompt.prompt_jp: なんで あなたに ___ なきゃいけないんだ？
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb-form fits 'why do I have to be bossed around by you?'

feedback.correct_en: The passive 指図される ('be ordered around') is what he resents — being told what to do BY her (あなたに marks the agent).
feedback.incorrect_en: The active forms would mean HE is ordering her — the opposite of what he's complaining about.

contrast_examples.jp: 人に指図されたくない。
contrast_examples.en: I don't want to be bossed around.
I give orders to my subordinates.

prompt.context_jp: シャツ選びをめぐって。
prompt.prompt_jp: あなたが文句をつけるから ___ んですよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Which form conveys 'I had no choice but to change it'?

choices.text: 替えざるをえなかった
替えてはいけなかった

feedback.correct_en: 〜ざるをえない means 'have no choice but to' — exactly fits 'I had to change it because you complained.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 替えたかった ('wanted to change') contradicts his resentful tone; 替えてはいけなかった ('shouldn't have') means the opposite.

contrast_examples.en: I have no choice but to go.
I can't help but admit it.

prompt.context_jp: みちるが桑野と夏美の口論を見て。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「___ ってやつです」(夫婦喧嘩について)
prompt.prompt_en: Which idiom means 'even a dog wouldn't touch it' (said of couples' quarrels)?

feedback.correct_en: 夫婦喧嘩は犬も食わない: 'even a dog won't eat a couple's quarrel' — meaning outsiders should stay out of it.
feedback.incorrect_en: 猫をかぶる means 'to pretend to be nice'; 馬の耳に念仏 means 'falling on deaf ears' — neither fits a lovers' quarrel.

contrast_examples.jp: 夫婦喧嘩は犬も食わない。
彼女は猫をかぶっている。
contrast_examples.en: She's putting on a demure act.

prompt.context_jp: 桑野が疲れた顔で現れる。
prompt.prompt_jp: あれ？ ___ 悪いですね。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word means 'you look pale/unwell'?

feedback.correct_en: 顔色が悪い is the fixed phrase for 'looking pale/unwell' (literally 'face-color is bad').
feedback.incorrect_en: 気分が悪い means 'feeling sick' (internal state, not visible); 機嫌が悪い means 'in a bad mood.'

contrast_examples.en: You look pale — are you okay?
They seem to be in a bad mood.

prompt.context_jp: 夏美の譬え話。
prompt.prompt_jp: 私たちの会話は キャッチボールじゃなくて ___ ばっかりだった気がします。
prompt.prompt_en: What sport metaphor fits 'just hitting the other person and ending it'?

feedback.correct_en: ドッジボール (dodgeball) is thrown TO HIT the other side — perfectly matches her 'our words only hit each other' complaint.
feedback.incorrect_en: The other sports involve cooperation or scoring, not the 'hit and done' image she wants to contrast with catch-ball dialogue.

contrast_examples.jp: 会話はキャッチボールだ。
contrast_examples.en: A conversation is a game of catch.

contrast_examples.jp: ドッジボールみたいな口げんか。

prompt.context_jp: 新聞勧誘を断る桑野。
prompt.prompt_jp: ゆうべも言いましたが ___ ます。
prompt.prompt_en: Which polite phrase declines a sales offer with 'I'm all set / no thanks'?

feedback.correct_en: 間に合ってます is a standard polite refusal — 'I already have enough / I'm covered.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 遅れる means 'be late' and 急ぐ means 'hurry' — neither declines an offer.

contrast_examples.jp: もう間に合ってますので、結構です。

contrast_examples.en: I made the train on time.

prompt.context_jp: 夏美が自分の望みを桑野に伝える場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural for conveying 'I want to play catch with YOU'?

choices.text: 私は キャッチボールがしてみたいです あなたと。
私が キャッチボールをしてみたいです あなたを。
私に キャッチボールはしてみたいです あなたが。

feedback.correct_en: A matches the actual line. 私は sets her up as topic; キャッチボールが with 〜したい is the standard pattern; あなたと for the partner.
feedback.incorrect_en: B uses を for the partner (should be と) and sounds like a self-promoting answer. C misuses に and が entirely.

contrast_examples.jp: 友達とキャッチボールがしたい。
contrast_examples.en: I want to play catch with a friend.
I want to talk with you.

prompt.context_jp: 二人がお互いに招待を遠回しに受ける場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds most natural for the drama's 'tsundere' phrasing 'well, if you really insist, I guess I could'?

choices.text: あなたが どうしてもって言うなら 行ってもいいですよ。
あなたは どうしてもって言うから 行くしかないです。
あなたを どうしてもって言ったら 行きたいです。

feedback.correct_en: A matches the series' signature line. 〜が…と言うなら + 〜てもいい gives the perfect reluctant-but-willing nuance.
feedback.incorrect_en: B sounds forced ('no choice but to go') and loses the coy tone; C has broken grammar (あなたを言う).

contrast_examples.jp: あなたがそう言うなら、行きます。
contrast_examples.en: If you say so, I'll go.

contrast_examples.jp: どうしてもと言うなら考えます。
contrast_examples.en: If you really insist, I'll consider it.

prompt.context_jp: 桑野が母に反発するような言い方。
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds most natural for 'you don't need to worry about ME'?

choices.text: 俺の心配なんて しなくていいでしょう？
俺が心配なんて しなくていいでしょう？
俺に心配なんて しなくていいでしょう？

feedback.correct_en: A matches the source. 俺の心配 ('worry about me') uses の for the object of the worry — a noun-noun relationship.
feedback.incorrect_en: B makes 'I' the one doing the worrying (wrong meaning); C sounds like he's 'worrying at' someone, which doesn't fit.

contrast_examples.jp: 息子の心配ばかりしている。
contrast_examples.en: She only worries about her son.

prompt.context_jp: 桑野の遠回しな愛情表現と夏美の返事。
prompt.prompt_en: Which exchange sounds most natural in the drama's understated register?

choices.text: ダメですか？ 僕じゃ／いいかもしれません
ダメですか？ 僕じゃ／はい、ダメです
ダメですか？ 僕が／いい思います

feedback.correct_en: A matches the source: 僕じゃダメですか is the humble 'am I not good enough?' phrasing, and いいかもしれません keeps her coy register.
feedback.incorrect_en: B flatly rejects (opposite meaning); C has grammatical slips (僕が and いい思います is malformed).

contrast_examples.jp: いいかもしれませんね。

prompt.context_jp: 母が将来について楽観的に答える。
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds most natural for 'it'll work out somehow'?

choices.text: なるようになりますよ。
なれるようになりますよ。
なりようになりますよ。

feedback.correct_en: なるようになる is the fixed idiom 'what will be, will be.' A matches the source.
feedback.incorrect_en: B uses the potential なれる (wrong form), and C is ungrammatical (なりよう is not the right nominalization here).

contrast_examples.jp: 心配しないで、なるようになるから。
人生はなるようになる。
